output.name: Halvúra
output.myth: On the longest night, when the sun is a thin thread, the old women build the Long Night Fire. My grandmother says it was lit from one spark that fell off Aun's knife the day he cut the string. He was sorry, and the spark was all he could carry home. He gave it to Hesk, who set it in a clay bowl and kept it turning so the wind could not take it. Tavo came down laughing and blew on it, and it only grew. Down in the south Minsa, the Child's Kite, watches it over the water, her string still running out. Up in the north-east Sekar, who swam under the grey floes until the light turned blue, keeps the bowl in his eye. Every hearth on the islands takes a coal before the year turns. Ennu says you must never let it out. The bowl is still up there, burning, and the Gulls carry its heat down to us every winter, passed hand to hand like a cup.
output.finding: Find Minsa, the Child's Kite, low in the south, and the Long Night Fire lies one hand-span straight north of her, on the Lamp Road.
